title: Evaluation of ChatGPT-Generated Simplifications of Shoulder MRI Reports: Assessments by Orthopedic Surgeons and Non-Healthcare Volunteers.
desc: [Diagnostics (Basel, Switzerland)] Background/Objectives: To evaluate ChatGPT-generated (GPT-5) simplifications of shoulder MRI reports from the perspectives of orthopedic surgeons and non-healthcare volunteers. Methods: In this single-center retrospective study, 100 de-identified shoulder MRI reports issued between June 2024 and June 2025 were simplified with ChatGPT in February 2026 using a standardized prompt. Between 10 March and 10 April 2026, three orthopedic surgeons independently rated each simplified text against the original report for accuracy, completeness, understandability, and misleading potential on a 5-point Likert scale (higher scores indicating better ratings). In a second arm, 100 adult non-healthcare volunteers each reviewed one simplified report and completed a six-item questionnaire on perceived clarity, comprehensibility, usefulness, and appropriateness. Results: Median expert scores were 5.0 in all domains, and all three raters assigned scores ≥ 4 in 86-98% of reports. Gwet's AC2 ranged from 0.93 to 0.98, whereas Krippendorff's α ranged from -0.02 to 0.05. Among volunteers, agreement ranged from 47% for understanding report terms to 80% for the appropriateness of the text. Health literacy correlated positively with most items (r = 0.329-0.429, p ≤ 0.001), and age correlated negatively with understanding report terms (r = -0.352, p < 0.001). Conclusions: The simplified reports were rated favorably by orthopedic surgeons and were perceived as useful by non-healthcare volunteers. However, the study was limited by its single-center design, the use of a single model and prompt, the absence of a comparison with the original reports in the volunteer arm, and the reliance on self-reported rather than objectively tested comprehension; therefore, it does not demonstrate improved patient comprehension or clinical safety. Such texts should supplement, not replace, the original report and physician consultation.

title: AI-Based Multi-View Echocardiographic Image Synthesis using Dynamic Shape Control
desc: Although automated methods have improved echocardiographic workflows, progress remains constrained by the need for large, well-annotated datasets. As the development of clinical databases is often limited by ethical and logistical challenges, synthetic data generation has emerged as a promising alternative. However, existing approaches commonly rely on left ventricle shape-based supervision or are tailored to specific cardiac views, limiting the generation of additional standard and unconventional imaging planes and the preservation of multi-view consistency across cardiac chambers. To address these limitations, we propose a novel framework for shape-controlled synthesis of multi-view echocardiographic sequences. First, multi-view cross-sections are extracted from dynamic whole-heart meshes. Ultrasound-like appearance is then introduced through a two-stage AI-based pipeline. In Stage 1, an unpaired GAN-diffusion model translates these cross-sections into realistic echocardiographic frames. As this translation is performed independently at the frame level, Stage 2 employs masked video reconstruction to improve temporal coherence and cardiac motion. Evaluation demonstrated high frame-level realism for both stages, while the integration of Stage 2 substantially improved video-level motion quality and temporal consistency. Overall, the proposed framework enables the generation of realistic multi-view echocardiographic sequences from diverse cardiac models, providing a scalable source of annotated data for dataset augmentation and the development of multi-view cardiac assessment methods.

title: HyM 2 Surv: Hypergraph learning for cross-magnification and microbiome-attentive multimodal survival prediction
desc: Publication date: January 2027 Source: Medical Image Analysis, Volume 115 Author(s): Fengyun Zhang, Kaimiao Hu, Changming Sun, Xiaofeng Liu, Leyi Wei, Ran Su

title: Evo2VED: a database of DNA large language model-derived scores for variant interpretation.
desc: [Nucleic acids research] The Evo2 Variant Effect Database (Evo2VED; https://dnallmved.org/) is a publicly accessible resource cataloging precomputed Evo2-derived variant effect scores, defined as allelic score differences, for 6.48 million human variants common in the gnomAD non-Finnish European population. Evo2VED includes scores from the 7B and 40B models under three scoring schemes, alongside annotations of variant function, evolutionary constraint, allele age, and disease associations. It integrates genome-wide association study (GWAS) data from UK Biobank, FinnGen, and the Million Veteran Program. Three complementary modules support variant-level interpretation, regional and region-set exploration, and trait-level analysis through flexible queries, interactive visualizations, and downloadable results. Evo2VED also catalogs associations between Evo2 annotations and per-SNP heritability across thousands of traits from these biobanks. A guided workflow connects GWAS with associated regions and individual variant evidence. Case studies of hypertension and depression illustrate how regional comparisons of Evo2 scores and GWAS signals can guide candidate variant prioritization. Evaluations using massively parallel reporter assays, molecular QTLs, fine-mapping probabilities, and clinical annotations assess associations with Evo2 scores alone and their added value beyond conservation and regulatory annotations. By providing accessible scores, contextual annotations, and comparative analyses, Evo2VED facilitates exploration and application of genomic language model predictions in human genetics research.

title: When evaluation becomes intervention in clinical AI
desc: AI judges, models that grade another system's output against a rubric, extend clinical review to the scale at which clinical AI writes. When teams use judge assessments to select a prompt or train a model, the judge becomes part of the intervention. Selection can then favor errors the judge overlooks. We describe what a judge's report must contain and the independent clinical test each judge-driven change needs.

title: Learning curve analysis of artificial intelligence-assisted ultrasound for teaching popliteal fossa sciatic nerve block to novice anesthesiologists: a pilot randomized educational study.
desc: [PeerJ] Artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted ultrasound may improve ultrasound-guided regional nerve blocks, but its effect on novice learning curves is unclear. In this pilot randomized educational study (June-August 2025), inexperienced anesthesiology residents from Shanghai General Hospital were assigned to AI-assisted or conventional training groups. The AI group used an ultrasound system with an AI module and received additional ethics and principles training, while the conventional group received standard training. Image acquisition and interpretation, debriefing time, trainee speaking time, and feedback were evaluated. Twenty-one trainee anesthesiologists were recruited (AI, n = 10; conventional, n = 11). The group-level cumulative sum (CUSUM) analysis identified an estimated turning point (TP) at approximately 12 attempts in the AI group. No comparable TP was identified within the 15-attempt training period in the conventional group. No statistically significant between-group differences were detected in participant-level phase-specific success rates (all P > 0.05). Compared with the conventional group, the AI group reported higher post-training feedback scores for training content (4.7 ± 0.5 vs. 3.6 ± 1.0, P = 0.0076), satisfaction (4.9 ± 0.3 vs. 3.5 ± 0.8, P < 0.0001), and confidence (5.0 ± 0.0 vs. 4.5 ± 0.7, P = 0.0216). Compared with the conventional group, the AI group also had a shorter participant-level mean debriefing time (7.33 ± 0.34 vs. 10.65 ± 0.61 min, P < 0.0001) and a greater proportion of trainee speaking time during debriefing (69.5% (65.70, 70.55) vs. 49.0% (46.70, 49.70), P < 0.0001). AI-assisted ultrasound training might enhance post-training feedback, increase satisfaction and confidence, and reduce debriefing time among inexperienced anesthesiology residents, suggesting its potential utility in the medical education of ultrasound.

title: Which Model, For Which Variable? Per-Variable Forecast Combination in Sparse ICU Time Series
desc: Clinical forecasting papers typically report a single best architecture. We show that on multivariate ICU physiology this question conceals variable-specific differences: no architecture is best on every variable, and which model wins changes from variable to variable. Across five ICU databases (MIMIC-III, MIMIC-IV, eICU, HiRID, and UMM (University Medicine Mannheim), a German single-center ICU) we forecast 94 channels over a 24-hour horizon with a pool of 14 models, and combine them with weights fitted per variable. On test, the combination beats the best single model on all five databases by 6.1-11.0% mean squared error (mean 8.7%). The gain is concentrated where clinical data is thinnest: the sparsest third of channels improves by 11.9% and laboratory values by 7.5%, against 3.1% for the densest third. Rank-based harmonic weighting of the best five models per variable, with no fitted weights at all, recovers about four-fifths of the gain. Extending the pool afterwards with a per-channel gradient-boosted tree, ARIMA and ETS makes the tree the validation-selected best single model on all five databases; per-variable combination still improves on it by 2.9-5.9% (significant on four of five), while equal weighting of the same members does not. As on univariate benchmarks, learned combination beats simple averaging - but only once the weights are constrained. We also report which model to prefer when, and show that the ordering changes with database size.

title: Explainable deep learning localizes age-discriminative candidate regions on hand radiographs of adult women.
desc: [Skeletal radiology] To determine whether deep learning can distinguish younger from older adult women on hand radiographs and to identify candidate anatomical regions for age-group discrimination using explainable artificial intelligence and quantitative cortical measurements. This retrospective, single-center, exploratory study included 2,221 women sampled consecutively within each age group during 2020-2023 (1,134 aged 20-45 and 1,087 aged 55-80 years at radiography). Patients contributed one posteroanterior radiograph and were assigned to mutually exclusive training, validation, or test sets. Five architectures were evaluated on the same 334 held-out test radiographs (171 younger; 163 older), with performance averaged across five random-seed runs. DenseNet121 was selected by descriptive comparison for gradient-weighted class activation mapping (Grad-CAM) and ray-based analyses with retraining. Manual cortical measurements of test radiographs yielded metacarpal and proximal phalangeal indices for candidate rays identified by Grad-CAM. DenseNet121 achieved the highest mean area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC, 0.996; 95% CI, 0.992-0.999). Grad-CAM showed prominent activation around the third proximal phalanx, with additional activation in the second and fourth rays. Performance remained high after ray masking; the third-ray-only model achieved the highest mean accuracy among single-ray models. The third proximal phalangeal index had the highest AUC among the six indices (0.956; 95% CI, 0.937-0.976). Grad-CAM, ray-based analyses, and quantitative cortical measurements support the third proximal phalanx as an anatomically interpretable candidate region for age-group discrimination in adult women. Integrating explainable artificial intelligence with quantitative radiographic assessment provides an exploratory workflow for investigating hand skeletal aging, with potential relevance to broader musculoskeletal imaging research.

title: Interpretable weight-space programming builds transparent transformers and brain encoding models
desc: Neural networks are powerful predictors, yet their opacity limits their usefulness in science, where the goal is explanation rather than mere prediction. In neuroscience, for example, deep encoding models accurately predict brain activity in response to natural stimuli, but struggle to reveal which stimulus features drive those predictions. Here we introduce interpretable weight-space programming (iWSP), a method in which an LLM agent iteratively builds interpretable models by explicitly programming their weights and features in code, without gradient-based training (backpropagation). Without backpropagation to tune parameters, the agent must draw on its prior knowledge and reason over previous trials to hypothesize, hand-craft, and refine human-interpretable computations mirroring the workflow of a human scientist. LLM audits confirm the interpretability of the hand-crafted models. We first validate iWSP by tasking it with constructing transformers for canonical benchmarks such as arithmetic and sentiment classification, finding that LLM agents can successfully craft compact, accurate networks directly. Next, we apply iWSP to build neural encoding models across vision, language, and audition. In the visual cortex, iWSP outpredicts existing interpretable baselines, uncovers distinct computations across early/higher visual areas, and generalizes to unseen data. In language fMRI, iWSP surfaces a confound in the data and in auditory ECoG, it systematically discovers interpretable acoustic features that predict neural activity. Together, these results establish iWSP as a general paradigm for aligning high predictive performance with human-interpretable scientific discovery.

title: Predicting Chiral Crystallization of Molecules Without Stereocenters.
desc: [Molecules (Basel, Switzerland)] Given an achiral molecule which lacks a stereocenter, will it form chiral crystals? Predicting the crystallization symmetry mode of molecules has long been a central challenge in structural chemistry. Particularly enigmatic has been the observation that achiral molecules can give rise to chiral crystals, assuming any of the 65 Sohncke space groups. While case-specific interpretations have been proposed over the years, no general and reliable predictive model for that phenomenon has emerged. Here, we present an efficient solution to this long-standing challenge. We do so by developing a high-accuracy artificial intelligence-based framework, capable of predicting whether an organic molecule lacking stereocenters will form either chiral or achiral crystals. With a carefully curated dataset of organic molecules devoid of stereocenters, we trained a supervised neural network classifier to predict whether such molecules crystallize in Sohncke or non-Sohncke space groups, while identifying the molecular descriptor patterns that favor each outcome. The model achieved a receiver operating characteristic area under the curve (ROC-AUC) of 0.954 on a balanced held-out test set drawn from the same data source. Analysis of the descriptors that most influence the model's predictions identifies molecular features that are statistically associated with each outcome. Predictions of the crystallization mode of anthracene and helicene derivatives exemplify these principles and are discussed in detail. Altogether, our predictive model opens new pathways for the rational design of molecules capable of forming chiral crystals and innovative avenues for crystal engineering, tailored for the many applications of chiral crystals, ranging from enantiomorphic drug safety considerations to enantioselective catalysis, and more.

title: Towards Explainable Sleep Stage Classification using Single-Channel Electroencephalogram
desc: Automated sleep staging has achieved strong bench- mark accuracy; however, clinical adoption remains limited due to a lack of interpretability. In this work, we fill the research gap by extending the SleepXAI sleep staging framework to systematically compare five different XAI methods. Further, attribution fidelity is evaluated using Spearman rank correlation with AASM-defined EEG frequency bands, serving as clinically grounded reference signals. In this paper, we focus on single- channel Electroencephalogram (EEG), which is more amenable to practical clinical deployment compared to full polysomnography setups. Experiments are conducted on the Sleep-EDF benchmark dataset and the DREAMT dataset. In DREAMT, we stratified subjects based on OSA into four Apnea-Hypopnea Index (AHI) severity groups. We observed that the SleepXAI model achieves strong classification performance on both datasets. Among the evaluated methods, Integrated Gradients (IG) consistently achieves the highest mean attribution fidelity across all five sleep stages on Sleep-EDF and across all AHI groups on DREAMT, outperforming all other evaluated methods under the Spearman rank correlation metric. These findings highlight the importance of attribution method selection as a key factor for ensuring reliable and clinically interpretable automated sleep staging systems.

title: Deep Learning-Based Classification of Pulmonary Hypertension Using Early-Fused CTPA and Pulmonary Artery Segmentation Maps.
desc: [Pulmonary circulation] Computed tomography pulmonary angiography (CTPA) is vital for diagnosing pulmonary hypertension (PH), especially thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension (CTEPH). However, manual image interpretation of CTPA often leads to misdiagnosis. This study aims to automatically segment the pulmonary artery from CTPA images and develop a deep learning model by fusing CTPA images with pulmonary artery segmentation results to distinguish pulmonary hypertension (PH vs. subjects without PH (no-PH)) and its PH subtype, CTEPH (CTEPH, other PH vs. no-PH). The study included 92 patients with CTEPH, 85 patients with other types of PH, and 140 no-PH. We completed the image preprocessing and segmentation of the pulmonary arterial tree of all the sample data. Based on four deep learning model classifiers-ResNet50, DenseNet, SENet, and Swin Transformer, we respectively developed four distinct network architectures: Single input channel for CTPA images, as well as early, middle, and late fusion strategies that combine CTPA images with their corresponding pulmonary vascular segmentation maps. The performance of the testing experiments has shown that the DenseNet (CTPA-seg) early fusion model achieves optimal performance in the binary classification task of pulmonary hypertension (PH vs. no-PH), with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.927. Meanwhile, the Swin Transformer (CTPA-seg) early fusion model shows the best performance in the ternary classification of pulmonary hypertension subtypes (CTEPH, other PH vs. no-PH), achieving an AUC of 0.855. Compared with models that only use clinical images, the early feature fusion strategy shows significantly higher accuracy in classifying and diagnosing PH, which is beneficial for the differential diagnosis of CTEPH.

title: NER-D: A cross-domain benchmark for German NER
desc: We present NER-D, a cross-domain benchmark for German NER comprising 13 datasets spanning 9 domains, including General/Politics, Wikipedia, Legal, Medical, Historical, Financial, Agriculture and Archaeology. We examine the performance of both proprietary LLMs and state-of-the-art small open-source models using normal prompting and further examine the performance gains achievable via in-context learning and LoRA fine-tuning. Our results show that without any sort of optimization a proprietary model (GPT-5.4 mini) outperforms the smaller open-source models on 6 out of 13 datasets, but LoRA fine-tuning enables the smaller models to substantially outperform the proprietary baseline. We further analyze the influence of the domain and the tagset used in each task on the performance achieved in the different evaluation settings. Our benchmark will be available as a resource for the development of future German NER methods on both general and specialized domains.\footnote{We make our code, data, and models publicly available upon acceptance of this paper.

title: Modeling distinct pathogenesis of early- and late-onset preeclampsia via hierarchical representation learning of interactome.
desc: [Briefings in bioinformatics] We developed and validated the pathogenesis models by hierarchical representation learning of interactomes connecting endometrial maturation, placentation, chorioamnionitis, and hemolysis, elevated liver enzyme, and low platelet (HELLP) syndrome. We utilized 19 gene sets from our previous work to infer interactomes to develop (n = 177) and validate (n = 352) explainable artificial intelligence models for each preeclampsia subtype using deep-insight visible neural network, gradient-weighted class activation mapping, and large language model. The hierarchically learned representations identified novel genes for late-onset preeclampsia (LOPE), similar to chorioamnionitis (ANKRD13A, SLA), and HELLP syndrome (PDE5A). We also identified novel genes for early-onset preeclampsia (EOPE), similar to HELLP syndrome (SWAP70, GREM2, GPR146, PIP5K1B, EZR). Our pathogenesis models connected HELLP syndrome with both LOPE and EOPE. However, chorioamnionitis was only connected with LOPE.

title: Vessel2Brain: Edge-Aware Multi-Scale Flow Matching for 3D Brain Image Generation from Vessel Masks
desc: Generating realistic 3D brain MRI volumes from sparse anatomical priors is a highly ill-posed yet clinically valuable problem, with important applications in data augmentation, simulation, and downstream neuroimaging analysis. In this work, we investigate the challenging task of synthesising full 3D brain MRI volumes conditioned solely on vascular label maps. While vascular structures provide strong anatomical and topological cues, they occupy only a small fraction of the brain volume and offer no direct information about surrounding tissue appearance. To address this challenge, we propose Vessel2Brain, an edge-aware multi-scale conditional flow matching framework that explicitly incorporates vascular structure information into the generative process. Our approach formulates vessel-guided brain image synthesis as a conditional continuous flow, enabling stable training and flexible generation while preserving structural correspondence. A multi-scale flow matching strategy is introduced to jointly model global anatomical coherence and fine-grained local details, with auxiliary velocity predictions providing additional supervision across spatial resolutions. Furthermore, we design an edge-aware objective that emphasises vascular boundaries during training, encouraging anatomically faithful tissue synthesis around vessel structures. We evaluate Vessel2Brain on two public 3D brain MRI datasets with paired vascular annotations. Extensive quantitative and qualitative experiments demonstrate that our method consistently outperforms state-of-the-art generative models in terms of reconstruction accuracy, structural consistency, and distributional realism.

title: Benchmarking Large Language Models for Sentiment Analysis in Pregnancy-Related Weight Discussions on Reddit: Human Performance-Aligned Comparative Evaluation Study.
desc: [JMIR formative research] Pregnancy-related weight gain is both physiologically complex and socially charged, and online discussions often combine clinical information with implicit emotional distress. Although automated sentiment analysis could support research on pregnancy-related discourse, model performance in this context remains inadequately characterized relative to expert human judgment. This study aimed to benchmark contemporary sentiment classification models on pregnancy-related weight discussions, with emphasis on agreement with expert consensus, interpretive ambiguity, task adaptation, and deployment across posts and comments. We curated 15,619 Reddit posts and comments using a large language model (LLM)-guided keyword expansion strategy and established an adjudicated consensus reference set of 200 posts. We evaluated 10 models on a fixed held-out test set (N=150) using aligned text inputs, weighted performance metrics, and 1000-resample bootstrap CIs. RoBERTa (Robustly Optimized Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers Approach) and BERTweet (Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers for Tweets) were additionally evaluated in a 5-fold fine-tuning sensitivity analysis. Gemini-3-Flash (Google DeepMind [Google LLC]) and Generative Pretrained Transformer (GPT)-OSS (OpenAI) were then applied to 400 unlabeled posts and 15,019 comments with intermodel agreement assessment. To expand expert-labeled coverage, a separate 106-post annotation extension was used for secondary evaluation of the 2 models carried forward to post-level corpus inference, and cross-source recoverability of the API-derived retrieval was assessed using Arctic Shift (Arthur Heitmann). The 2 primary experts (FAK and BMW) achieved 59.0% preadjudication agreement (Cohen κ=0.344). In the fixed held-out comparison, Gemini-3-Flash had the numerically highest weighted F1-score of 0.662 (κ=0.478), followed by GPT-OSS (F1-score=0.645; κ=0.436), with overlapping CIs across leading models. Under the harmonized direct-argmax decision rule with minimally processed text, BERTweet achieved an F1-score of 0.623 (κ=0.369), and RoBERTa achieved an F1-score of 0.605 (κ=0.339). In the separate fine-tuning sensitivity analysis, the mean cross-validated F1-score was 0.708 (SD 0.087) for RoBERTa and 0.616 (SD 0.079) for BERTweet. Among Gemini-3-Flash errors, 55.8% (29/52) occurred in posts on which the 2 primary experts disagreed. In the 106-post annotation extension, primary-expert agreement was 64.

title: Naegele's rule is not a 280-day count: generative AI conflates two distinct pregnancy-dating algorithms.
desc: [Journal of perinatal medicine] Naegele's calendar rule and an exact 280-day count are commonly treated as equivalent methods for estimating the due date (EDD), although their calendar arithmetic differs. We quantified this difference and evaluated whether generative artificial intelligence (AI) systems disclosed and accurately labeled the method used. A deterministic script calculated EDDs for every last menstrual period (LMP) date from January 1, 1812, through December 31, 2025, using Naegele's calendar rule and a fixed 280-day count. Five generative AI systems answered four prespecified LMP prompts, representing agreement and differences of 1, 2, and 3 days. Each prompt was submitted in three separate conversations, yielding 60 responses. Among 78,163 LMP dates, the methods produced identical EDDs in 34,609 cases (44.3 %) and different EDDs in 43,554 (55.7 %). Naegele's calendar rule produced dates 1 day later in 27.0 %, 2 days later in 21.0 %, and 3 days later in 7.7 %. The methods never agreed among 14,828 intervals containing February 29. Of 60 AI responses, 57 (95.0 %) included the exact 280-day date and 48 (80.0 %) stated a calculation method. Only 18 of 45 responses to divergent dates distinguished the algorithms. Twelve of 48 method-stating responses contained a method-label mismatch. Naegele's calendar rule and fixed 280-day counting are distinct algorithms. Their small numerical differences are unlikely to be clinically important, but they provide a deterministic test of computational transparency. Generative AI systems should disclose the calculation used, distinguish non-equivalent methods, and label them accurately.

title: X-VAD: Video Anomaly Detection with Kinematic Explanations.
desc: [Sensors (Basel, Switzerland)] Anomaly scores alone do not describe unusual motion. X-VAD links scoring and reporting through 13 cell-level kinematic descriptors from SEA-RAFT optical flow. They describe speed, direction, flow deformation, and temporal change. Each vector is compared with normal training observations from the same cell. The four highest calibrated cell scores are averaged to obtain the frame score. No gradient-based training of an anomaly scorer is required. Rule-based alarm reports identify the region, descriptor deviations, and nearest normal reference. YOLO-World adds object context without changing the score. Micro-averaged area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) reaches 85.78%, 84.42%, and 75.43% on UCSD Ped2, CUHK Avenue, and IITB-Corridor, respectively. At the 0.85 threshold, all stored test scores yield true-positive rates of 87.69%, 90.78%, and 62.73%. Corresponding false-positive rates are 41.46%, 46.32%, and 26.53%. Runtime measurements use an NVIDIA A100-SXM4-40GB at batch size 1. Mean score-availability times are 50.0, 50.6, and 82.6 ms per frame pair, excluding frame reading. Report generation, including YOLO-World inference, adds 16.3-18.3 ms per alarm frame on average. Visualization and notification delivery are excluded. The IITB-Corridor AUROC approaches VideoPatchCore's 76.4%.X-VAD provides inspectable motion reports, although its AUROCs trail SETJiP on Ped2 (99.3%) and AI-VAD on Avenue (93.7%).

title: Eyes in the Wild and Minds in the Loop: A Systematic Review of Artificial Intelligence for Camera-Trap Wildlife Monitoring.
desc: [Sensors (Basel, Switzerland)] Camera traps generate imagery faster than people can review it, and artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly used to analyse it. This systematic review asks to what extent AI applied to camera-trap imagery has moved from benchmark performance to ecologically usable monitoring. Following PRISMA 2020, Scopus was searched on 6 August 2026 for 2020-2026. Peer-reviewed English-language journal articles applying automated inference to imagery from unattended cameras observing free-ranging animals were included; captive or web-sourced imagery, non-image methods, reviews and conference papers were excluded. Of 637 records, 231 were read in full and 201 were included. Studies were appraised against six quality criteria, findings were synthesised as descriptive counts across five research questions, and performance was tabulated on each study's own metric, without meta-analysis. Output grew by about 29% per year. Detection and species classification each appear in 62% of studies, behaviour recognition in 5%, and study regions invert global biodiversity gradients. Only 62% of studies evaluate beyond their training data, a share unchanged since 2020; the measured generalisation penalty ranges from six to nearly seventy points. Only 35% report field deployment; costs appear only in deployment-oriented studies. The gap between benchmark performance and ecological practice remains the field's central challenge.

title: From Observational Biology to Functional and Computable Models of Living Systems.
desc: [Cancer innovation] The proposed framework moves from fragmented biological evidence toward testable, computable life functions that describe how biological states evolve over time. A stepwise experimental approach progresses from molecular processes to unicellular and multicellular models, with tumor systems serving as models of pathological state transitions. The graphical image was Created with BioRender.com (Ji L. 2026; https://BioRender.com/zaxq2dd).

title: RAID: Retrieval Augmented Intrusion Detection for Cyber Physical Systems.
desc: [Sensors (Basel, Switzerland)] This paper presents a Retrieval Augmented Intrusion Detection system (RAID), a three-stage framework for interpretable AI-driven intrusion detection in Industrial Control Systems (ICS). Existing ICS detectors flag anomalies without explaining them, and LLM-based explanations are rarely verified against the detector's rules or linked to past incidents. Specifically, a resilient isolation forest algorithm is used for its ability to generate structured anomaly interpretations and to mitigate the effects of dangerous data drift. A grounded physics-aware feature engineering process extends the baseline capabilities of this algorithm, including counterfactual evaluation, contrastive analysis, causal chain identification, and redundancy inspection of data streams. Subsequently, a fleet of Large Language Models (LLMs) is used to generate deep natural-language explanations for each anomaly log, under the guidance of an independent LLM orchestrator that produces a final incident report. Finally, a Retrieval-Augmented Generation framework embeds the historical patterns of the recovered events into an accessible index that contains all the log interpretations over time. The entire framework is validated at each stage on the HAI-21.03 dataset: among nine unsupervised detectors, the Isolation Forest provides the most balanced performance (F1 = 0.409, MCC = 0.393, eTaPR F1 = 0.773); 87% of the propositions generated by the language agents exactly match the underlying detection rules; and the retrieval stage reaches 0.998 faithfulness and 0.782 answer correctness.

title: The Evaluation of Developmental Dysplasia of Hip from Pediatric Ultrasound Images by Key Point-Based Deep Learning.
desc: [Diagnostics (Basel, Switzerland)] Background: Developmental dysplasia of the hip (DDH) is a common hip disorder in infants. Ultrasound is the primary imaging modality for infants younger than 6 months, but measurements using the Graf and Harcke methods depend on examiner experience. This study aimed to develop and internally validate a key point-based deep learning model for the automated measurement of the Graf α and β angles and femoral head coverage. Methods: A total of 300 standard-plane hip ultrasound images from 165 infants aged 0-6 months were retrospectively collected at a single tertiary center, and reference key points were determined by consensus of pediatric orthopedic surgeons. We developed a dual-branch network, named "DDH-KPNet," which combines a UNet++ convolutional branch and a transformer branch fused with attention modules. Performance was evaluated with fivefold cross-validation at three levels: accuracy of key point localization; intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC); and DDH classification. Results: The experimental results demonstrated that Graf-based classification achieved accuracy = 0.903, sensitivity = 0.81, and specificity = 0.9497 (under 95% conference interval); Harcke classification achieved accuracy = 0.942, sensitivity = 0.888, and specificity = 0.968 (under 95% conference interval); and ICCs for α = 0.832, β = 0.728, and coverage = 0.923. Conclusions: The proposed model showed promising agreement with expert measurements under internal validation. Multicenter external validation and independent diagnostic analysis by different physicians are required before clinical implementation.

title: The Europe-Asia-Pacific Divide in Atrial Fibrillation Management: Evidence, Practice, and Policy.
desc: [JACC. Asia] Atrial fibrillation affects approximately 60 million people worldwide, and Europe and the Asia-Pacific region together carry most of that burden. This state-of-the-art review compares the 2 regions across 6 domains: epidemiology and risk factors, lifestyle and comorbidity management, stroke prevention, rhythm control and catheter ablation, digital health and artificial intelligence-electrocardiogram, and health system infrastructure and policy. Practice diverges in all 6. European management follows European Society of Cardiology guidelines, whereas Asia-Pacific region care varies across socioeconomic settings and rests on population-scale evidence, with region-wide guidance so far limited to topic-specific Asia Pacific Heart Rhythm Society (APHRS) consensus statements until the first APHRS guideline was released in 2026. Anticoagulation gaps have narrowed in both regions, yet disparities in financing, electrophysiology capacity, and digital access persist, and differences within each region rival those between them. Closing these gaps requires region-specific, resource-adapted strategies and mutual adoption of evidence generated in each region.
